successCriteria.description: scripts/smoke.js, after stage 3d, seeds a second leave type (LeaveTypeCode.SICK) with an effective ACTIVE policy and NO leave_balances row, and seeds a bcrypt password_hash for the seeded employee — without weakening, deleting, or reordering stages 1–3d.
A new stage logs in via POST /auth/login with the seeded employee's email/password and asserts the response carries a non-empty token and a profile whose id/email/role match the seeded employee.

A new stage calls GET /employees/me with the login token and asserts the returned profile matches the seeded employee (id, employeeNumber, email, role, hireDate serialized as UTC midnight, and null managerId/department).
A new stage calls GET /leaves with the login token and asserts the leave request created in stage 3d is present in the returned list.
A new stage calls GET /leaves/:id using the id captured from the POST /leaves response body and asserts the seeded request is returned.

A new stage calls GET /balances/me with the login token and asserts the result contains EXACTLY the seeded current-period balance and omits the second leave type (which has an effective policy but no balance row).

constraints: The seeded current-period balance for stage (e) must be computed with periodContaining(hireDate, 12, new Date()) so its periodStart/periodEnd fall in the CURRENT accrual period — GET /balances/me uses asOf = new Date(), so the existing 2030–2031 bal-1 will NOT be returned and must not be relied upon.

The second leave type must be seeded as a leave_types row plus an effective leave_policies row (status ACTIVE, effective_from <= now, effective_to null) with NO leave_balances row — this is what proves getCurrentBalances omits an effective policy lacking a balance.

The seeded employee's password_hash must be produced with bcrypt.hashSync('<plaintext>', 10) and the SAME plaintext used in POST /auth/login, because AuthService.login compares via bcrypt.compare(password, employee.passwordHash ?? '').
The leave request id for stage (d) must be captured from the POST /leaves response body (authed.json().id), not predicted — the repository generates it with randomUUID().
The new stages must assert real values (token presence, profile fields, list membership, balance contents), not merely status codes.
The new stages must run only in Postgres mode (SMOKE_DATABASE_URL set), consistent with stage 3d's persistence gate; in sqlite mode they must be skipped with the existing caveat rather than failing.
JWT_SECRET must be set to a known value before boot so the login token verifies under the same secret the app's registerAuth uses; signToken is already imported and available.
outOfScope: Implementing GET /employees/me route (src/modules/employee/employee.routes.ts, src/modules/employee/index.ts, src/app.ts) — owned by Sub-phase 7.1.
Unit tests for auth service and leave routes (tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts, tests/unit/modules/auth/auth.service.test.ts) — owned by Sub-phase 7.3.
Creating any Jest test files or requiring test existence/coverage as a success criterion for this sub-phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: The profile returned by login and /employees/me has exactly the 10 fields of EmployeeProfile (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, role, managerId, department, hireDate, employmentStatus) and never exposes passwordHash or terminationDate; managerId and department are null when not seeded.

getCurrentBalances returns at most one balance per leaveTypeCode, only for leave types that have BOTH an effective ACTIVE policy and a balance row in the current accrual period; a leave type with an effective policy but no balance row is omitted (never synthesized, never throws).
The seeded leave request created in stage 3d is visible to its owner via list and getById (EMPLOYEE role scoping to employeeIds=[actor.id]).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Public (no token required); returns a token and the caller's EmployeeProfile on valid credentials.
Requires a valid bearer token; returns the authenticated employee's profile (never passwordHash).
Requires a valid bearer token; EMPLOYEE sees only their own requests.
Requires a valid bearer token; returns the request only if the caller may see it, otherwise NotFoundError identical to a nonexistent id.
Requires a valid bearer token; returns the caller's current-period balances, omitting leave types with no balance row.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The seeded current-period balance must match the period boundaries getCurrentBalances computes via periodContaining(employee.hireDate, policy.accrualPeriodMonths, new Date()) — reuse the same periodContaining from src/shared/date rather than hardcoding dates.
The seeded employee's password_hash must satisfy AuthService.login's bcrypt.compare(password, employee.passwordHash ?? '') — hash with bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10) and reuse the same plaintext.
The profile assertions must match the EmployeeProfile shape produced by toEmployeeProfile (10 fields, no passwordHash/terminationDate, null managerId/department when unseeded).
The login token must be minted/verified under the same JWT_SECRET the app's registerAuth uses; signToken is imported from src/shared/auth and the secret must be set before boot.
DATE columns (hireDate, periodStart/periodEnd, startDate/endDate) serialize as UTC-midnight strings (e.g. "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z") — assertions must compare against that serialization.
The second leave type's policy must satisfy getCurrentBalances' effective-policy selection (status === LeavePolicyStatus.ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= now, effectiveTo null or >= now).

integrationPoints.why: The smoke check exercises the real login path end-to-end; the seeded password_hash must satisfy its bcrypt.compare.
Stage (e) verifies the current-period balance selection and the omission of an effective policy with no balance row.
The login token must verify under the same JWT_SECRET the app's preHandler uses.
Stages (c) and (d) verify EMPLOYEE role scoping returns the seeded request.
